subject.title: feat(gateway): land remaining durable-approvals stack and repair main gates

question: Should unresolved plugin approvals fail closed unconditionally even for existing plugins that set `timeoutBehavior: "allow"`, or should that compatibility behavior remain available behind an explicit temporary policy?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes a shipped plugin API field's runtime effect at the execution-authorization boundary; automation can verify either implementation but cannot choose the permanent security-versus-upgrade contract.

options.title: Keep unconditional fail-closed
options.body: Retain the deprecated field for source compatibility but never let timeout or missing approval release execution authority, with clear upgrade notes and focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Add temporary compatibility policy
options.body: Preserve the former behavior only through an explicit opt-in policy with a deprecation and removal plan, while keeping the default fail-closed.

recommendation.title: Keep unconditional fail-closed
recommendation.body: Retain the deprecated field for source compatibility but never let timeout or missing approval release execution authority, with clear upgrade notes and focused compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the durable approval architecture and authored the fail-closed integration whose permanent compatibility contract needs confirmation.
